 DES Moines, Iowa — Iowa residents who need help paying winter heating bills can apply for the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program, or LIHEAP, through their local community action agency.
 Applications opened Oct. 1 for people 60 and older and people with disabilities. Applications for all other eligible households will be accepted from Nov. 1 through April 30, 2027.
 To qualify, a household’s income must be at or below 200% of the 2026 federal poverty guidelines. The annual gross income limit is $31,920 for a one-person household and $66,000 for a family of four.
 Eligible residents can find a local community action outreach office through Iowa Community Action Association . The Iowa Department of Health and Human Services also has program information online , and residents can call 211 for eligibility information.
 MidAmerican Energy encourages customers who receive a disconnection notice to call 888-427-5632 to discuss payment arrangements and assistance options.
 Customers can also use MidAmerican’s Budget Billing program to make monthly bills more predictable. Donations to the company’s I CARE program help local community action agencies pay heating bills and provide home weatherization for low-income residents.
